name: Lacy Lunsford
subject: You could be the difference between a strong legal defense and my husband spending the next 11 years in prison.
body:
I'm a wife and a mother, not an activist. But today I'm asking for your help because the man I love is facing the fight of his life.
| [View in Web Browser](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e947327/VaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvYkg2YlhBdnJjNw/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMTA/LbmNsZEFCdXZLbA/qP2hpZHM9bmNZbHFTanhXSW5LNERscw/gavMobQ/scr72b458e3)
| |
---
| | | Dear Fellow Patriot, I never imagined I would be writing a letter like this. I'm a wife and a mother, not an activist. But today I'm asking for your help because the man I love is facing the fight of his life. My husband, Officer Brad Lunsford, will soon be back in court defending himself against charges that never should have been brought in the first place. And the legal bills continue to pile up. [**That's why I'm asking you to make a generous contribution to the Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund (LELDF) today.**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.) Brad has spent his entire adult life serving others. He's a proud Army combat veteran. A devoted husband and father. And for more than ten years, he served as a police officer with the Las Cruces Police Department. Then one afternoon everything changed. A robbery suspect attacked Brad's partner and knocked him to the pavement. During the struggle, the suspect gained control of the officer's taser and pointed it directly at him. In a matter of seconds, Brad was forced to make the decision no officer ever wants to make. He fired a single shot. His partner survived and went home to his wife and newborn baby. But our family's nightmare was only beginning. Because more than a year later, Attorney General Raul Torrez charged Brad with manslaughter. **To put New Mexico politics into context for you – Torrez is notoriously anti-cop and his campaign was bankrolled by leftist billionaire George Soros.** _The same George Soros who, for the past decade, has spent tens of millions of dollars installing his hand-picked, police-hating puppets into prosecutors’ offices across America._ What followed was a trial filled with troubling questions and irregularities that ultimately resulted in Brad's conviction – **including a juror who failed to disclose their ties to Black Lives Matter.** Since the trial was overturned, Torrez and his junior Attorney General, R. John Duran II, have doubled down his desire to see my husband behind bars – and will use the full resources of the state government to finish the job. Now we're preparing for the next chapter of this fight. And we can't do it alone. **[That’s why I’m asking you to donate $25, $50, $100, or more to LELDF today.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** For over 30 years, LELDF has helped wrongly accused and convicted officers, like Brad, clear their names and win back their freedoms. From trials to appeals, and even presidential pardons, LELDF has a long track record of success. But they don’t receive taxpayer funding or grants, and large gifts are few and far between. Instead, LELDF relies on people like you who are sick and tired of progressive prosecutors trying to ruin the lives of good officers with bogus charges and witch-hunts. Brad’s first trial cost hundreds of thousands of dollars. With the games Torrez’s office is playing, we anticipate a second trial will cost even more. But your gift today ensures Brad receives the legal defense he deserves – not only at trial, but during this critical waiting period when Brad’s attorneys work to get the case dismissed. And believe me, they are working hard filing motions and investigating the corruption! [**So, can I count on you to make a generous, tax-deductible donation to LELDF today?**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.) Remember, the prosecution has unlimited taxpayer resources. Brad does not. Your gift today could be the difference between a strong defense and the next 11 years in prison. Thank you in advance for standing with my husband and backing the blue. Gratefully,
---
**_Lacy Lunsford_**
---
| | | [ **Support the Lunsford Family** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
|
---
_More such officers who sacrifice so much for will face similar fates unless we speak out and stand up for the brave men and women in blue. The next time you see a police officer in your community, please thank them for their service. To read more about our mission or the other Law Enforcement officers we're defending, please visit www.leldf.org. And remember - Blue Lives Matter!_ [**Join our sustaining members by making a monthly gift to LELDF today!**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

**Tuesday, November 10, 2026**
On Monday, November 2, we sat at the kitchen table with the sample ballot between us.
_Yes or no on Amendment 3?_
The choice had been framed as financial relief or community sacrifice. We considered what either vote might mean for our family.
After it passed, a Facebook conversation brought our county into view. Some neighbors welcomed the relief; others feared what might be lost. Different circumstances, different conclusions, but a shared concern for the financial future of our community.
We will not always agree, but we can come to the American kitchen table, take stock of what we have, and make the best of it together.
Sometimes that means finding the sweet ground.
**Pause.
Breathe.
Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

**Tuesday, November 10, 2026 - **
_**Iran:** Two tankers on fire in Hormuz after using "unauthorised route," IRGC says. Trump says Iran war "militarily is effectively over." GCC establishes military HQ in Kuwait. France accuses IRGC of October cyberattacks on refrigerators and freezers._

Al Jazeera: UK grants contracts to companies linked to Israeli settlements. Petition for public inquiry into UK complicity in Gaza genocide passes 100,000 signatures, triggering parliamentary consideration._
_**Yemen:** Saudi airstrikes on Sana'a kill one person. Yemeni rights group: Over 30 killed in Ansarallah attacks in Taiz over three days. Saudi pipeline targeted._
_**Lebanon:** Israel attacks Lebanon, again violating so-called ceasefire._
_**U.S.:** Trump social-media strategist accused of unregistered Qatar work. Democrat Scott Colom maintains lead in Mississippi Senate race. California voters reject proposed "billionaire tax." Supreme Court clears the way for border construction in Texas' Big Bend region. Senate facilitates data-center permitting in first legislation advanced since midterms. Another ranking DOJ attorney resigns. Despite increasing Dem discontent, Jeffries says he is "confident" he will be elected House speaker. Sen. Chris Van Hollen says hasn't ruled out challenging Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader. Palestinian socialist Ahmed Moor announces 2028 primary challenge to Sen. John Fetterman. TAP: Trump administration looks to install former subprime autolender in key regulatory role._
_**International:** Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta ends operations after pressure from authorities. France raises minimum wage 1.6% in attempt to quell protests. Hungarian police arrest brother of Viktor Orban. 2,500+ people flee Darfur for Chad. Gunmen kill guard and 10 relatives, abduct 13 in northwest Nigeria. # Iran
* **Two tankers on fire in Hormuz after using "unauthorised route," IRGC says:** The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Crops (IRGC) said on Tuesday that two oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after using what it said was an "unauthorised route."
* In a statement, the IRGC said, "One of these vessels, a supertanker, hit a naval mine and exploded, and the second tanker, which was under the protection of the US aggressor's fighter jets and was attempting to secretly pass through the illegal route, had an accident and was stopped in its place with a terrible fire."
* **Trump says Iran war "militarily is effectively over": **President Donald Trump [said](https://substack.com/redirect/aef60a2d-4ab3-489c-8904-b952bfb707c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Monday that the Iran war is "militarily effectively over," while signaling that the U.S. blockade would continue. Trump's announcement follows talks with Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani in Washington, DC.
* Speaking at a news conference, Trump said "Iran militarily is effectively over. We're just keeping it the status quo, and we're doing that really at the behest of countries that are their neighbors." He added, "We just had, just in case, another aircraft carrier. We have many. Sailing over and just arriving in the Middle East, so we have three. And they're all locked and loaded, and hopefully we don't have to use them."
* In a phone interview with C-SPAN on Monday, Trump also claimed that Iran wanted to reach an agreement with Washington. "They want to make a deal. They don't say that, you know, publicly," he said. "In speaking with Qatar--as you know, the prime minister was in the Oval Office today--in speaking to Saudi Arabia, UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait ... they'd rather do it this way rather than another hit, which would be approximately five times bigger than the first hit."
* Iranian Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei denied Trump's claims that Iran was seeking a deal. "The war on Iran has already wrecked the U.S. government. But Washington flails like a desperate gambler. FOLD YOUR HAND. STOP manufacturing FAKE NEWS about imaginary talks. Stop denying the West Asian NEW ORDER," Rezaei wrote in a [post](https://substack.com/redirect/1b78de7c-e811-4857-9d05-84632d3e651b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on X.
* **GCC establishes military HQ in Kuwait:** Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) member states approved the establishment of an advanced headquarters for their unified military command in Kuwait and the deployment of forces to the facility, GCC Secretary-General Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi said in a statement.
* "These directives reflect a firm Gulf commitment to safeguarding the security and sovereignty of the GCC states and strengthening their ability to confront common threats," Albudaiwi added.
* **France accuses IRGC of October cyberattacks on refrigerators and freezers:** On Monday, France [accused](https://substack.com/redirect/7757a35e-af5a-4e52-b081-5e4ff810fc93?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Iran of orchestrating cyberattacks that knocked out hundreds of commercial refrigerators and freezers at French supermarkets in October. French officials said that there would be "consequences" for the attack. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said that he summoned the Iranian ambassador and threatened further European Union sanctions against Iran. On October 11, a series of hacks targeted 700 commercial sites in France, sparking at least 15 fires. A second series of hacks this month hit more than 100 European establishments, including French blood-bank refrigerators.

# Palestine
* **Three killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza on Tuesday:** Two Palestinians were killed, including a child, and several people were wounded in an Israeli air strike on a shelter in the Zeitoun neighborhood of Gaza City on Tuesday, Al Jazeera reported. Separately, a Palestinian was killed by Israeli gunfire in Khan Younis.
* Over the past 24 hours, Israeli attacks killed one Palestinian and injured 16 others across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. One body was also recovered from under the rubble.
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023, has risen to 74,645 killed and 175,978 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,614 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,849, while 850 bodies have been recovered.
* **Israeli settlers and soldiers simultaneously raid Beita, in occupied West Bank:** On Monday, dozens of Israeli settlers [stormed](https://substack.com/redirect/2bed355e-fb7d-48ce-90df-b4955cb71992?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an industrial zone in Beita, south of Nablus, and set fire to three bulldozers, several other vehicles, and equipment belonging to stone-cutting workshops, WAFA reported. Israeli forces raided the town simultaneously.
* Settlers have repeatedly attacked Beita's industrial zone, burning facilities and vehicles and opening fire on Palestinians.
* Settler attacks across the occupied West Bank more than doubled in October to 1,369, with 353 in the Nablus governorate alone, according to the Palestinian Authority's Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission.
* **Settlers attack Palestinian farmers:** Israeli settlers blocked Palestinian farmers from reaching their olive groves near Silwad, east of Ramallah, on Monday.
* Settlers also attacked farmers picking olives near the town's cemetery and forced them off their land, WAFA reported.
* **Al Jazeera: UK grants contracts to companies linked to Israeli settlements:** The United Kingdom has awarded 10.7 million pounds (around $14.4 million) in new public contracts to companies with links to illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank, despite the British government's recent pledge to punish companies that profit from settlement activity, an Al Jazeera [investigation](https://substack.com/redirect/9a32f608-dce5-49d6-baf0-1a87f26db43d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) found. The contracts were publicized following UK sanctions on Israeli settlements in September. At the time, the UK government said it would take action against companies aiding settlement expansion.
* **Petition for public inquiry into UK complicity in Gaza genocide passes 100,000 signatures, triggering parliamentary consideration:** A petition on the UK Parliament's website that [calls](https://substack.com/redirect/5987e0b2-ddd1-49d3-9757-d4dd736a9c05?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for a public investigation into British government complicity in the Gaza genocide passed 100,000 signatures on Monday, requiring Parliament to formally consider the measure. The petition specifically demands that the inquiry empower investigators to question government ministers and officials, and to uncover "the sale, supply, or use of weapons, surveillance aircraft, and Royal Air Force bases" in support of the genocide. The petition was launched by Jennifer Forbes, a member of Your Party, the left-wing party headed in Parliament by Jeremy Corbyn. In 2024, an Al Jazeera investigation found that the UK created an air bridge supporting Israel's war, and that UK firms supplied jet parts to the Israeli military.

# Yemen
* **Saudi airstrikes on Sana 'a kill one person: **A Saudi-led coalition airstrike hit a gas station in Sana'a on Tuesday, killing one person and injuring three others, according to the spokesperson for the health ministry in Sana'a.
* Another Saudi-coalition airstrike targeted an oil company building in the capital, injuring at least six people, causing "extensive damage" to nearby homes and shops.
* Ansarallah said that Saudi-led strikes targeted sites in several governorates on Monday and Tuesday, including Hodeidah and Saada.
* **Yemeni rights group: Over 30 killed in Ansarallah attacks in Taiz over three days:** At least 33 civilians have been killed and 58 others wounded in attacks by Ansarallah in the governorate of Taiz over the past 73 hours, the Yemeni Network for Rights and Freedoms said on Monday.
* The rights group documented 133 violations against civilians and civilian infrastructure, including 216 projectiles fired at residential areas.
* The group also blamed Ansarallah for an attack on a market in Al-Waziiya district on Friday, which it said killed at least 30 people and wounded 45 others. Ansarallah blamed Saudi Arabia for the attack.
* **Saudi pipeline targeted:** Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline in the Medina region was "targeted" on Monday, sparking a "limited fire" that was quickly extinguished, the Saudi Energy Ministry said. There were no casualties, and oil operations continued. The ministry did not say who carried out the attack, and no group claimed responsibility for it as of Monday night.
* Separately, satellite images on November 8 show "possible signs of damage" at Pumping Station 8 along the pipeline, according to the satellite-imagery firm Soar Atlas. The roughly 1,200 km pipeline carries about 4 million barrels a day to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz.

# Lebanon
* **Israel attacks Lebanon, again violating so-called ceasefire:** Israeli fighter jets attacked the town of Qantara on Tuesday, according to Al Jazeera. Footage shows smoke billowing at the scene. Israeli forces also fired toward the outskirts of the town of Chaqra, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. The towns of al-Mansouri and Majdal Zoun were also targeted by Israeli artillery.

# U.S. News
* **Trump social-media strategist accused of unregistered Qatar work: Derek Utley,** a co-founder of the digital strategy firm X Strategies, filed a lawsuit in Florida on Monday [accusing](https://substack.com/redirect/341c30db-babf-4263-a9d8-1c7bdf9f0293?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**** his former partner, **Alex Bruesewitz** ,**** of accepting $500,000 from "individuals associated with Qatar," arguing that he violated federal law by failing to disclose the payments. He is a senior adviser to President Trump's primary leadership PAC, Never Surrender. In that work, he runs the popular social-media accounts @TrumpWarRoom and @TeamTrump. Through a lawyer, Bruesewitz denied the claims in Utley's complaint.
* **Democrat Scott Colom maintains lead in Mississippi Senate race:** Mississippi's**** Democratic Senate candidate **Scott Colom** [remains](https://substack.com/redirect/59afd5bb-b45a-4a00-957b-ee7a19a9d110?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ahead of incumbent Republican Sen. **Cindy Hyde-Smith** , leading by 2,574 votes, according to a Monday tally from the Associated Press. Mississippi Secretary of State **Michael Watson** said that about 2,800 absentee ballots still need to be counted, most of which are from the Democrat-leaning counties of Hinds and Holmes. Mississippi does not have a mechanism for an automatic vote recount, meaning that a losing candidate must file a lawsuit to gain one.
* **California voters reject proposed "billionaire tax": **California voters [rejected](https://substack.com/redirect/5337f722-acd3-43fd-af5e-24d9f635dafc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Proposition 40, a ballot proposition that would have imposed a one-time 5% tax on residents whose net worth exceeds $1 billion, the AP reported on Monday. Organized opposition to the proposition was widespread. Google co-founder **Sergey Brin** donated more than $100 million to a PAC opposed to the proposition. Gov. **Gavin Newsom** , a possible 2028 presidential candidate, opposed it, as did Planned Parenthood and the California Medical Association. Sen. **Bernie Sanders**(D-Vt.)**** campaigned for it. The "Yes on 40" campaign said that it may return the measure to the ballot in 2028.
* **Supreme Court clears the way for border construction in Texas ' Big Bend region: **The Supreme Court [lifted](https://substack.com/redirect/11ac81d7-6945-435f-b656-4a7f0d822165?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a federal judge's recent halt on construction in Texas' Big Bend region on Monday, allowing the Trump administration to move forward with its planned expansion of border security and surveillance measures along a roughly 500-mile stretch of the U.S.-Mexico border. A legal challenge to the project is still wending its way through the courts. Only Justice **Ketanji Brown Jackson** noted her dissent to Monday's decision. The plaintiffs in the ongoing case against the project include an environmental group, local preservationists, a river guide, and a landowner. The Trump administration previously dropped plans for a wall inside Big Bend National Park, opting instead for the construction of patrol roads, vehicle barriers, and surveillance infrastructure.
* **Senate facilitates data-center permitting in first legislation advanced since midterms:** The Senate voted to formally [take up](https://substack.com/redirect/f5995f19-908b-459e-846d-1cd2c71416be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a bill on Monday that would streamline environmental permitting for data centers. The legislation would shorten approval timelines for large, energy-intensive projects, while requiring owners of data centers to pay for the energy they use. The bill was negotiated before the election by Republican Sens. **Shelley Moore Capito**(W. Va.) and **Mike Lee** (Utah), and Democratic Sens. **Martin Heinrich** (N.M.) and **Sheldon Whitehouse**(R.I.). Trump expressed support for the bill in a post on social media on Sunday. Environmental groups like the Sierra Club and National Wildlife Federation have strongly opposed its passage.
* **Another ranking DOJ attorney resigns: Brett Shumate** , the head of the Justice Department's civil division, [resigned](https://substack.com/redirect/a49814fa-2c37-48ca-b05d-87a5975aaf69?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Monday.**** The civil division represents the government in most litigation, defending federal policies and presidential actions, and handling fraud and immigration enforcement cases. Shumate is the latest DOJ departure since the midterms. Other DOJ officials who have recently resigned include Civil Rights Division chief **Harmeet Dhillon** , National Security Division head **John Eisenberg,** and veteran litigator **Henry Whitaker** , an aide to Attorney General **Todd Blanche**.
* **Despite increasing Dem discontent, Jeffries says he is "confident" he will be elected House speaker: **House Minority Leader **Hakeem Jeffries**(N.Y.) [told](https://substack.com/redirect/d4029121-f29d-40a3-99aa-e469e2f3f311?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) reporters on Monday that he is "confident" he will be elected speaker of the House in January. * **Sen. # Other International News
* **Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta ends operations after pressure from authorities:** The Russian investigative newspaper Novaya Gazeta [held](https://substack.com/redirect/bf1361b5-8dc4-4ab8-827d-1d0da1c1a486?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its last editorial meeting on Monday and closed its Moscow newsroom. It announced in October that it was being forced to shut down after the government designated it a "foreign agent," and cut its access to the Russian banking system. Authorities arrested an editor at the paper, Oleg Roldugin, in April, and last month they searched the home of editor-in-chief Sergei Sokolov and questioned him. UN rights chief Volker Turk called Russia's crackdown on the publication "yet another devastating blow for remaining independent media" in the country. Novaya Gazeta was co-founded by Mikhail Gorbachev and funded with money from his Nobel Peace Prize. The paper was one of the few outlets that openly criticized Russia's war in Ukraine.
* **France raises minimum wage 1.6% in attempt to quell protests:** France will raise the minimum wage by 1.6% on December 1, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/7757a35e-af5a-4e52-b081-5e4ff810fc93?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Monday, expediting an increase that was scheduled for January 2027. The increase raises the monthly minimum wage by 24 euros ($27), from 1,477.93 euros ($1,656) to 1,502 euros ($1,683). Lecornu told reporters this was "the second-largest rise in 20 years" and "not merely symbolic." It falls short of trade unions' demands, however. The French Democratic Confederation of Labour wants a raise of at least 100 euros, and the General Confederation of Labour has demanded a raise of about 150 euros. CGT head Sophie Binet called Monday's raise "crumbs."
* **Hungarian police arrest brother of Viktor Orb an: **Hungarian police [arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/173a2520-b0db-4889-9dcd-ae18322dcf7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Viktor Orban's younger brother Aron on Monday, on suspicion of "people smuggling" and other offenses, according to a press report shared by Prime Minister Peter Magyar. Viktor Orban wrote on X that he was "the real target" of the arrest. A 2025 investigation by the news site Telex linked Aron Orban and others to an alleged scheme involving visas for foreign guest workers. Magyar, who won the premiership in a landslide election in April, promised to investigate his predecessor's alleged corruption and abuse of power.
* **2,500+ people flee Darfur for Chad:** A harvest failure, insufficient rainfall, and the ongoing civil war have [forced](https://substack.com/redirect/d0375c5c-485c-47e6-9a34-81b298b37595?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 2,510 people to flee Darfur for Chad, the Sudan Tribune reported. Adam Rijal, a spokesperson for the General Coordination of Displaced Persons and Refugees, said that living conditions in Darfur are rapidly deteriorating. He said that the region desperately needs a surge in all kinds of aid--food, water, and medicine.
* **Gunmen kill guard and 10 relatives, abduct 13 in northwest Nigeria:** Gunmen [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/8464131e-15ce-40d2-821b-bbbc8b0dd9ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a local security volunteer and 10 of his relatives in an attack in Nigeria's northwestern Zamfara state over the weekend, torching his house and abducting a further 13 relatives, Reuters reported. A police official said that the security guard, a member of a government-backed vigilante group, had helped state security forces fend off gang incursions in the area, leading the "bandits" to consider him "an obstacle to their activities." Security forces have been deployed to secure the hostages' release. Armed gangs have long raided villages in northwestern Nigeria, killing residents, abducting people for ransom, and looting homes.
* **South African police arrest nine foreign nationals suspected of trying to join Russia 's war on Ukraine:** South African police [arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/0cd6fd23-0e29-4cb9-95c7-b876d81ffaa3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) nine young men, ages 20 to 26, at Johannesburg's OR Tambo Airport on Sunday night, accusing them of seeking to fight in Russia's war in Ukraine. The arrests follow an investigation involving Interpol and local agencies. South Africa's Regulation of Foreign Military Assistance Act bars mercenary activity, recruitment, and training. The arrests come amid concern that Africans, Asians, and South Americans are being lured to Russia with civilian job offers and forced into combat in Ukraine.
* **Paraguay expands probe of collapsed bank Ueno, agents raid bank office:** Paraguayan**** prosecutors [raided](https://substack.com/redirect/28f02d3c-4493-4fb0-b0ed-aa2b20cad9e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the digital bank Ueno's brokerage arm on Monday. The raid is part of a widening probe into Ueno, a huge bank whose collapse led to the resignation of Santiago Peña from the presidency last week. Following the raid, prosecutors shared images of ripped-up documents, including fragments of what appeared to be due-diligence reports and emails.
* Separately, Paraguay's Congress approved President Pedro Alliana's nomination of economist Jorge Schreiner to replace former central bank chief Carlos Carvallo on Tuesday. It also named the former banking regulator Fernando Rivarola, who warned the public about Ueno in a July report, to the board of the central bank. Like the former president Peña, Carvallo has business ties to Ueno. Both men were recently charged with breach of trust and administration and are in pretrial detention.
* **Exxon Mobil reaches preliminary, nonbinding deal with Venezuela:** ExxonMobil [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/ec1db7fa-a785-4cd7-8340-b829c62382d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Monday that it drafted a memorandum of understanding with Venezuela. The agreement is nonbinding, which allows Exxon to hedge its bets. The company said that "any future investment would require stable policies, clear regulations, strong investment protections and competitive returns." The deal is a symbolic win for Trump and a reversal of Exxon Mobil's position in January, when CEO Darren Woods called Venezuela "uninvestable." Venezuela has twice seized Exxon's assets in the country.
* **Taiwan accuses China of "area denial" drills in Western Pacific: **On Tuesday, Taiwanese**** Defense Minister Wellington Koo [accused](https://substack.com/redirect/617c06a2-1975-4142-b1d7-6d2f697dee5d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) China of conducting "area denial" drills in the Western Pacific. Koo told reporters that China used its Liaoning carrier group and other naval formations in the process. "Anti-access area denial" is a military tactic designed to deter outside forces from intervening in conflict. Last week, Taiwan's security chief Joseph Wu said that more than 100 Chinese naval and Coast Guard ships were operating in the South China Sea and in the Pacific, and the defense ministry reported a large rise in Chinese aircraft in the area. China did not respond to Tuesday's accusations, though its defense ministry said last month that the Liaoning carrier group's trainings are scheduled annually and are not aimed at any country.

Photo by Tatyana Makeyeva/AFP via Getty Images. Tuesday, November 10, 2026 - Iran: Two tankers on fire in Hormuz after using "unauthorised route," IRGC says. Trump says Iran war "militarily is effectively over." GCC establishes military HQ in Kuwait. France accuses IRGC of October cyberattacks on refrigerators and freezers. Al Jazeera: UK grants contracts to companies linked to Israeli settlements. Petition for public inquiry into UK complicity in Gaza genocide passes 100,000 signatures, triggering parliamentary consideration. Yemen: Saudi airstrikes on Sana'a kill one person. Yemeni rights group: Over 30 killed in Ansarallah attacks in Taiz over three days. Saudi pipeline targeted. Lebanon: Israel attacks Lebanon, again violating so-called ceasefire. U.S.: Trump social-media strategist accused of unregistered Qatar work. Democrat Scott Colom maintains lead in Mississippi Senate race. California voters reject proposed "billionaire tax." Supreme Court clears the way for border construction in Texas' Big Bend region. Senate facilitates data-center permitting in first legislation advanced since midterms. Chris Van Hollen says hasn't ruled out challenging Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader. Palestinian socialist Ahmed Moor announces 2028 primary challenge to Sen. John Fetterman. TAP: Trump administration looks to install former subprime autolender in key regulatory role. International: Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta ends operations after pressure from authorities. France raises minimum wage 1.6% in attempt to quell protests. Hungarian police arrest brother of Viktor Orban. 2,500+ people flee Darfur for Chad. Paraguay expands probe of collapsed bank Ueno, agents raid bank office. Exxon Mobil reaches preliminary, nonbinding deal with Venezuela. Taiwan accuses China of "area denial" drills in Western Pacific. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Two tankers on fire in Hormuz after using "unauthorised route," IRGC says: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Crops (IRGC) said on Tuesday that two oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after using what it said was an "unauthorised route." In a statement, the IRGC said, "One of these vessels, a supertanker, hit a naval mine and exploded, and the second tanker, which was under the protection of the US aggressor's fighter jets and was attempting to secretly pass through the illegal route, had an accident and was stopped in its place with a terrible fire." Trump says Iran war "militarily is effectively over": President Donald Trump on Monday that the Iran war is "militarily effectively over," while signaling that the U.S. blockade would continue. Trump's announcement follows talks with Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani in Washington, DC. Speaking at a news conference, Trump said "Iran militarily is effectively over. We're just keeping it the status quo, and we're doing that really at the behest of countries that are their neighbors." He added, "We just had, just in case, another aircraft carrier. We have many. Sailing over and just arriving in the Middle East, so we have three. And they're all locked and loaded, and hopefully we don't have to use them." In a phone interview with C-SPAN on Monday, Trump also claimed that Iran wanted to reach an agreement with Washington. "They want to make a deal. They don't say that, you know, publicly," he said. "In speaking with Qatar--as you know, the prime minister was in the Oval Office today--in speaking to Saudi Arabia, UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait ... they'd rather do it this way rather than another hit, which would be approximately five times bigger than the first hit." Iranian Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei denied Trump's claims that Iran was seeking a deal. "The war on Iran has already wrecked the U.S. government. But Washington flails like a desperate gambler. FOLD YOUR HAND. STOP manufacturing FAKE NEWS about imaginary talks. Stop denying the West Asian NEW ORDER," Rezaei wrote in a on X. GCC establishes military HQ in Kuwait: Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) member states approved the establishment of an advanced headquarters for their unified military command in Kuwait and the deployment of forces to the facility, GCC Secretary-General Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi said in a statement. "These directives reflect a firm Gulf commitment to safeguarding the security and sovereignty of the GCC states and strengthening their ability to confront common threats," Albudaiwi added. France accuses IRGC of October cyberattacks on refrigerators and freezers: On Monday, France Iran of orchestrating cyberattacks that knocked out hundreds of commercial refrigerators and freezers at French supermarkets in October. French officials said that there would be "consequences" for the attack. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said that he summoned the Iranian ambassador and threatened further European Union sanctions against Iran. On October 11, a series of hacks targeted 700 commercial sites in France, sparking at least 15 fires. A second series of hacks this month hit more than 100 European establishments, including French blood-bank refrigerators. Palestine Three killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza on Tuesday: Two Palestinians were killed, including a child, and several people were wounded in an Israeli air strike on a shelter in the Zeitoun neighborhood of Gaza City on Tuesday, Al Jazeera reported. Separately, a Palestinian was killed by Israeli gunfire in Khan Younis. Over the past 24 hours, Israeli attacks killed one Palestinian and injured 16 others across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. One body was also recovered from under the rubble. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023, has risen to 74,645 killed and 175,978 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,614 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,849, while 850 bodies have been recovered. Israeli settlers and soldiers simultaneously raid Beita, in occupied West Bank: On Monday, dozens of Israeli settlers an industrial zone in Beita, south of Nablus, and set fire to three bulldozers, several other vehicles, and equipment belonging to stone-cutting workshops, WAFA reported. Israeli forces raided the town simultaneously. Settlers have repeatedly attacked Beita's industrial zone, burning facilities and vehicles and opening fire on Palestinians. Settler attacks across the occupied West Bank more than doubled in October to 1,369, with 353 in the Nablus governorate alone, according to the Palestinian Authority's Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission. Settlers attack Palestinian farmers: Israeli settlers blocked Palestinian farmers from reaching their olive groves near Silwad, east of Ramallah, on Monday. Settlers also attacked farmers picking olives near the town's cemetery and forced them off their land, WAFA reported. Al Jazeera: UK grants contracts to companies linked to Israeli settlements: The United Kingdom has awarded 10.7 million pounds (around $14.4 million) in new public contracts to companies with links to illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank, despite the British government's recent pledge to punish companies that profit from settlement activity, an Al Jazeera found. The contracts were publicized following UK sanctions on Israeli settlements in September. At the time, the UK government said it would take action against companies aiding settlement expansion. Petition for public inquiry into UK complicity in Gaza genocide passes 100,000 signatures, triggering parliamentary consideration: A petition on the UK Parliament's website that for a public investigation into British government complicity in the Gaza genocide passed 100,000 signatures on Monday, requiring Parliament to formally consider the measure. The petition specifically demands that the inquiry empower investigators to question government ministers and officials, and to uncover "the sale, supply, or use of weapons, surveillance aircraft, and Royal Air Force bases" in support of the genocide. The petition was launched by Jennifer Forbes, a member of Your Party, the left-wing party headed in Parliament by Jeremy Corbyn. In 2024, an Al Jazeera investigation found that the UK created an air bridge supporting Israel's war, and that UK firms supplied jet parts to the Israeli military. Yemen Saudi airstrikes on Sana 'a kill one person: A Saudi-led coalition airstrike hit a gas station in Sana'a on Tuesday, killing one person and injuring three others, according to the spokesperson for the health ministry in Sana'a. Another Saudi-coalition airstrike targeted an oil company building in the capital, injuring at least six people, causing "extensive damage" to nearby homes and shops. Ansarallah said that Saudi-led strikes targeted sites in several governorates on Monday and Tuesday, including Hodeidah and Saada. Yemeni rights group: Over 30 killed in Ansarallah attacks in Taiz over three days: At least 33 civilians have been killed and 58 others wounded in attacks by Ansarallah in the governorate of Taiz over the past 73 hours, the Yemeni Network for Rights and Freedoms said on Monday. The rights group documented 133 violations against civilians and civilian infrastructure, including 216 projectiles fired at residential areas. The group also blamed Ansarallah for an attack on a market in Al-Waziiya district on Friday, which it said killed at least 30 people and wounded 45 others. Ansarallah blamed Saudi Arabia for the attack. Saudi pipeline targeted: Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline in the Medina region was "targeted" on Monday, sparking a "limited fire" that was quickly extinguished, the Saudi Energy Ministry said. There were no casualties, and oil operations continued. The ministry did not say who carried out the attack, and no group claimed responsibility for it as of Monday night. Separately, satellite images on November 8 show "possible signs of damage" at Pumping Station 8 along the pipeline, according to the satellite-imagery firm Soar Atlas. The roughly 1,200 km pipeline carries about 4 million barrels a day to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz. Lebanon Israel attacks Lebanon, again violating so-called ceasefire: Israeli fighter jets attacked the town of Qantara on Tuesday, according to Al Jazeera. Footage shows smoke billowing at the scene. Israeli forces also fired toward the outskirts of the town of Chaqra, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. The towns of al-Mansouri and Majdal Zoun were also targeted by Israeli artillery. U.S. News Trump social-media strategist accused of unregistered Qatar work: Derek Utley, a co-founder of the digital strategy firm X Strategies, filed a lawsuit in Florida on Monday ** his former partner, Alex Bruesewitz , of accepting $500,000 from "individuals associated with Qatar," arguing that he violated federal law by failing to disclose the payments. Bruesewitz, who continues to run X Strategies after an acrimonious split with Utley, worked as an aide on President Donald Trump's 2024 presidential campaign and continues to work on behalf of Republican causes and candidates. He is a senior adviser to President Trump's primary leadership PAC, Never Surrender. In that work, he runs the popular social-media accounts @TrumpWarRoom and @TeamTrump. Through a lawyer, Bruesewitz denied the claims in Utley's complaint. Democrat Scott Colom maintains lead in Mississippi Senate race: Mississippi's** Democratic Senate candidate Scott Colom ahead of incumbent Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith , leading by 2,574 votes, according to a Monday tally from the Associated Press. Mississippi election officials have until Tuesday to count provisional (affidavit) ballots and receive postmarked absentee ballots, and all 82 counties have until Friday to certify their results. Mississippi Secretary of State Michael Watson said that about 2,800 absentee ballots still need to be counted, most of which are from the Democrat-leaning counties of Hinds and Holmes. Mississippi does not have a mechanism for an automatic vote recount, meaning that a losing candidate must file a lawsuit to gain one. California voters reject proposed "billionaire tax": California voters Proposition 40, a ballot proposition that would have imposed a one-time 5% tax on residents whose net worth exceeds $1 billion, the AP reported on Monday. If it had passed, the taxed money would have supplemented the $100 billion that California is projected to lose as a result of federal healthcare cuts over the next five years. Organized opposition to the proposition was widespread. Google co-founder Sergey Brin donated more than $100 million to a PAC opposed to the proposition. Gov. Gavin Newsom , a possible 2028 presidential candidate, opposed it, as did Planned Parenthood and the California Medical Association. Sen. Bernie Sanders(D-Vt.)** campaigned for it. The "Yes on 40" campaign said that it may return the measure to the ballot in 2028. Supreme Court clears the way for border construction in Texas ' Big Bend region: The Supreme Court a federal judge's recent halt on construction in Texas' Big Bend region on Monday, allowing the Trump administration to move forward with its planned expansion of border security and surveillance measures along a roughly 500-mile stretch of the U.S.-Mexico border. A legal challenge to the project is still wending its way through the courts. Only Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson noted her dissent to Monday's decision. The plaintiffs in the ongoing case against the project include an environmental group, local preservationists, a river guide, and a landowner. The Trump administration previously dropped plans for a wall inside Big Bend National Park, opting instead for the construction of patrol roads, vehicle barriers, and surveillance infrastructure. Senate facilitates data-center permitting in first legislation advanced since midterms: The Senate voted to formally a bill on Monday that would streamline environmental permitting for data centers. The legislation would shorten approval timelines for large, energy-intensive projects, while requiring owners of data centers to pay for the energy they use. The bill was negotiated before the election by Republican Sens. Shelley Moore Capito(W. Va.) and Mike Lee (Utah), and Democratic Sens. Martin Heinrich (N.M.) and Sheldon Whitehouse(R.I.). Trump expressed support for the bill in a post on social media on Sunday. Environmental groups like the Sierra Club and National Wildlife Federation have strongly opposed its passage. Another ranking DOJ attorney resigns: Brett Shumate , the head of the Justice Department's civil division, on Monday.** The civil division represents the government in most litigation, defending federal policies and presidential actions, and handling fraud and immigration enforcement cases. Shumate is the latest DOJ departure since the midterms. Other DOJ officials who have recently resigned include Civil Rights Division chief Harmeet Dhillon , National Security Division head John Eisenberg, and veteran litigator Henry Whitaker , an aide to Attorney General Todd Blanche. Despite increasing Dem discontent, Jeffries says he is "confident" he will be elected House speaker: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries(N.Y.) reporters on Monday that he is "confident" he will be elected speaker of the House in January. He added that the Democratic Caucus will meet next Wednesday to choose its leader. To win the election for speaker, he will need to reach 218 votes. Democrats are expected to hold 254 seats in the next Congress. Reps.-elect Darializa Avila Chevalier(D-N.Y.) and Melat Kiros (D-Colo.) have expressed reluctance to support Jeffries. Chevalier said that she would prefer a speaker who will fight for "working-class people [and] Medicare for All." Kiros said that she would not vote for a speaker who accepts corporate PAC money, as Jeffries does. Other incoming Democratic representatives, including Richard Ojeda (N.C.) and Katy Padilla Stout (Texas), declined to endorse Jeffries. A public petition Jeffries to step aside has reached over 1 million signatures. Sen. Chris Van Hollen says hasn 't ruled out challenging Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader: Maryland Democrat Sen. Chris Van Hollen on Monday that the party "shouldn't have a coronation" for majority leader, and that he "hasn't shut the door" to a possible run for the position. Sen. Chuck Schumer , leader of the Democratic Senate Caucus since 2017, is widely expected to win enough support to become Senate majority leader in a closed-door vote in early December. Sen. Elissa Slotkin , who met with Van Hollen on Monday and hasn't ruled out her own run for the leadership role, said that she won't vote for a candidate who cannot articulate "a plan" for Democrats, especially for the first 100 days of the new Congress. Palestinian socialist Ahmed Moor announces 2028 primary challenge to Sen. John Fetterman: Ahmed Moor , a 42-year-old Palestinian American writer and member of the Democratic Socialists of America, that he will challenge Sen. John Fetterman (D-Penn.) in the 2028 primary. Fetterman is among Israel's most vociferous defenders in the Democratic Party, and he votes in alignment with the Trump agenda than any other Democratic legislator. Moor said that he is "not really running against Fetterman" but "for good government" and "the rule of law." TAP: Trump administration looks to install former subprime autolender in key regulatory role: The White House is attempting to appoint Christopher Mufarrige to the vacant Republican commissioner's seat on the Federal Trade Commission, The American Prospect . His nomination could be announced during a hearing of the Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee on Tuesday. Mufarrige ran a "buy here, pay here" used-car business in Texas called CNJ Auto Finance for three years in the late 2000s. Such businesses have been criticized for predatory tactics like imposing high interest rates on consumers who have poor credit, targeting consumers who publicly file for bankruptcy, and rapidly repossessing vehicles if consumers default on their loans. Mufarrige's firm was unsuccessfully sued twice, once for taking vehicles without proper payment and another time for failure to pay property taxes. TAP's full report is available . 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com. Other International News Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta ends operations after pressure from authorities: The Russian investigative newspaper Novaya Gazeta its last editorial meeting on Monday and closed its Moscow newsroom. It announced in October that it was being forced to shut down after the government designated it a "foreign agent," and cut its access to the Russian banking system. Authorities arrested an editor at the paper, Oleg Roldugin, in April, and last month they searched the home of editor-in-chief Sergei Sokolov and questioned him. UN rights chief Volker Turk called Russia's crackdown on the publication "yet another devastating blow for remaining independent media" in the country. Novaya Gazeta was co-founded by Mikhail Gorbachev and funded with money from his Nobel Peace Prize. The paper was one of the few outlets that openly criticized Russia's war in Ukraine. France raises minimum wage 1.6% in attempt to quell protests: France will raise the minimum wage by 1.6% on December 1, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu on Monday, expediting an increase that was scheduled for January 2027. The increase raises the monthly minimum wage by 24 euros ($27), from 1,477.93 euros ($1,656) to 1,502 euros ($1,683). Lecornu told reporters this was "the second-largest rise in 20 years" and "not merely symbolic." It falls short of trade unions' demands, however. The French Democratic Confederation of Labour wants a raise of at least 100 euros, and the General Confederation of Labour has demanded a raise of about 150 euros. CGT head Sophie Binet called Monday's raise "crumbs." Hungarian police arrest brother of Viktor Orb an: Hungarian police Viktor Orban's younger brother Aron on Monday, on suspicion of "people smuggling" and other offenses, according to a press report shared by Prime Minister Peter Magyar. Viktor Orban wrote on X that he was "the real target" of the arrest. A 2025 investigation by the news site Telex linked Aron Orban and others to an alleged scheme involving visas for foreign guest workers. Magyar, who won the premiership in a landslide election in April, promised to investigate his predecessor's alleged corruption and abuse of power. 2,500+ people flee Darfur for Chad: A harvest failure, insufficient rainfall, and the ongoing civil war have 2,510 people to flee Darfur for Chad, the Sudan Tribune reported. Adam Rijal, a spokesperson for the General Coordination of Displaced Persons and Refugees, said that living conditions in Darfur are rapidly deteriorating. He said that the region desperately needs a surge in all kinds of aid--food, water, and medicine. Gunmen kill guard and 10 relatives, abduct 13 in northwest Nigeria: Gunmen a local security volunteer and 10 of his relatives in an attack in Nigeria's northwestern Zamfara state over the weekend, torching his house and abducting a further 13 relatives, Reuters reported. A police official said that the security guard, a member of a government-backed vigilante group, had helped state security forces fend off gang incursions in the area, leading the "bandits" to consider him "an obstacle to their activities." Security forces have been deployed to secure the hostages' release. Armed gangs have long raided villages in northwestern Nigeria, killing residents, abducting people for ransom, and looting homes. South African police arrest nine foreign nationals suspected of trying to join Russia 's war on Ukraine: South African police nine young men, ages 20 to 26, at Johannesburg's OR Tambo Airport on Sunday night, accusing them of seeking to fight in Russia's war in Ukraine. The arrests follow an investigation involving Interpol and local agencies. South Africa's Regulation of Foreign Military Assistance Act bars mercenary activity, recruitment, and training. The arrests come amid concern that Africans, Asians, and South Americans are being lured to Russia with civilian job offers and forced into combat in Ukraine. Paraguay expands probe of collapsed bank Ueno, agents raid bank office: Paraguayan** prosecutors the digital bank Ueno's brokerage arm on Monday. The raid is part of a widening probe into Ueno, a huge bank whose collapse led to the resignation of Santiago Peña from the presidency last week. Following the raid, prosecutors shared images of ripped-up documents, including fragments of what appeared to be due-diligence reports and emails. Separately, Paraguay's Congress approved President Pedro Alliana's nomination of economist Jorge Schreiner to replace former central bank chief Carlos Carvallo on Tuesday. It also named the former banking regulator Fernando Rivarola, who warned the public about Ueno in a July report, to the board of the central bank. Like the former president Peña, Carvallo has business ties to Ueno. Both men were recently charged with breach of trust and administration and are in pretrial detention. Exxon Mobil reaches preliminary, nonbinding deal with Venezuela: ExxonMobil on Monday that it drafted a memorandum of understanding with Venezuela. The agreement is nonbinding, which allows Exxon to hedge its bets. The company said that "any future investment would require stable policies, clear regulations, strong investment protections and competitive returns." The deal is a symbolic win for Trump and a reversal of Exxon Mobil's position in January, when CEO Darren Woods called Venezuela "uninvestable." Venezuela has twice seized Exxon's assets in the country. Taiwan accuses China of "area denial" drills in Western Pacific: On Tuesday, Taiwanese** Defense Minister Wellington Koo China of conducting "area denial" drills in the Western Pacific. Koo told reporters that China used its Liaoning carrier group and other naval formations in the process. "Anti-access area denial" is a military tactic designed to deter outside forces from intervening in conflict. Last week, Taiwan's security chief Joseph Wu said that more than 100 Chinese naval and Coast Guard ships were operating in the South China Sea and in the Pacific, and the defense ministry reported a large rise in Chinese aircraft in the area. There's a line in _Hamilton_ where George Washington tells a young Alexander Hamilton, "Winning was easy, young man, governing's harder." It's a lesson Democrats would be wise to remember after Tuesday's historic election.
This was the [largest blue wave since Watergate](https://substack.com/redirect/efa3742f-fa2b-478c-acc0-c1e49f29e60d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). But Democrats should be careful not to mistake a rejection of Donald Trump's policies for an unconditional embrace of their own party's ideas. Many Americans who voted blue weren't necessarily voting _for_ Democrats so much as they were voting _against_ the direction of the country, particularly rising costs driven by tariffs and the war in Iran.
Democrats often talk about being a big-tent party. But as we saw last Tuesday in competitive races across red and purple states like Georgia and Texas, winning means reaching beyond the Democratic base and persuading independents and moderates that Democrats can do a better job of governing. Even Pope Leo voted in the election - the first Pope ever to vote in a US election.
The fact that so many independent Americans have placed their trust in Democrats to do a better job should be humbling, not an invitation to take a victory lap.
Consider that Tuesday marked the seventh consecutive federal election in which control of at least one of Washington's three elected institutions--the House, Senate, or White House--changed hands. Americans keep voting for change, only to find themselves demanding it again two years later. If Democrats want to break that cycle, they need to show Americans that their trust wasn't misplaced through action and not just words.
Democrats shouldn't wait until January to start proving they can deliver. The lame-duck session going on now and the next two years offer an opportunity to lower costs and rebuild public trust through bipartisan cooperation. There are already encouraging signs. James Talarico, the newly elected Democratic senator from Texas, has expressed a willingness to work with President Trump on border security and immigration reform. It's the kind of sentiment that would have been difficult to imagine from a Democrat during Trump's first administration.

---|---|---
**Chart from[Bruce Mehlman's Substack](https://substack.com/redirect/ff22dc9a-9ab0-4eca-b062-4c8e4cc99609?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Congress has several major pieces of legislation to address before the end of the year, giving Republicans and Democrats an opportunity to show Americans they can still work together. The most urgent is keeping the government open. Federal funding[ expires on December 11](https://substack.com/redirect/cd6f7929-a619-4951-b2f6-42822f1a8f33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and after enduring[ the longest government shutdown in American history](https://substack.com/redirect/ccbcfd84-5d53-4baf-ab43-158082f80cf6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) last year--43 days--The last thing we need is a repeat.
Lawmakers must also pass the annual[ National Defense Authorization Act](https://substack.com/redirect/3642ae91-736b-4602-9ba3-757e524a25a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (NDAA), which sets our nation's defense priorities and supports the readiness of the men and women serving in uniform.
Then there's permitting reform, which sounds about as exciting as watching paint dry, but has enormous consequences for American families and businesses. It takes four years on average to approve and connect new energy projects to the electrical grid, even as demand for electricity continues to grow. (They should've called my friend and messaging guru, Frank Luntz up at West Point for some advice.) One [recent analysis](https://substack.com/redirect/e5fbd59e-3fc5-4b01-a9d1-a2f3da2622f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) found that power plants completed in 2025 had waited a median of 61 months to connect to the grid, compared with 22 months in 2008. Streamlining these processes could help bring more affordable energy online (including clean power), strengthen domestic manufacturing, and improve our economic competitiveness. It's failed the last five years, but Semafor reports: "We believe we have the votes to proceed," said Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse, D-R.I. He said he believes the bill is also in "very good shape" in the House...The legislation aims to speed up big electricity projects and force data centers to pay for their share of electric grid usage. Its passage would represent a significant feat, considering the failed permitting efforts of the past five years. "We don't have to wait for a new Congress to start lowering costs," said Sen. Martin Heinrich, D-N.M.
And here's another seemingly mundane issue with surprisingly high stakes: sulfur. Yes, sulfur. That smelly stuff you vaguely remember from chemistry class is actually a matter of national security. It's essential to producing fertilizer, processing critical minerals, and manufacturing materials our military depends on. And as the war in Iran has reminded us, something as basic as sulfur can become a serious problem when global supply chains are disrupted. They're essential to protecting America's security and prosperity.
And we cannot talk seriously about affordability without addressing healthcare. Americans are already struggling with rising insurance premiums, and the average benchmark Affordable Care Act marketplace [premium is increasing another 13% in 2027](https://substack.com/redirect/aa2a95ed-37fe-4d2a-8201-9f2c28a802c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). That's on top of a 26% increase the previous year. Families shouldn't have to choose between paying for healthcare and keeping up with their other bills.
These are real problems requiring real solutions. They also present an opportunity for Republicans and Democrats to work across party lines and find common ground.
**The New Congress**
When the new Congress convenes in January, Democrats should arrive with a clear 100-hour and 100-day agenda focused on affordability, ethics, and restoring trust in government.
I know the value of such a plan firsthand. Twenty years ago, I was part of the Democratic majority elected to Congress in another historic wave. Thirty one of us arrived in Washington with a 100-hour agenda that included ethics reform (no revolving door lobbying or gifts), implementing the recommendations of the 9/11 Commission, and raising the federal minimum wage to $7.25 (which hasn't been raised federally since then). We understood that winning an election was only the beginning. Voters expected us to deliver. Here's me talking to Will Cain about earning trust back with action:
[](https://substack.com/redirect/3cdb865d-4a90-4c55-ad39-4539f1eb56e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Today's Democrats should approach their new majority with that same sense of urgency. That means pursuing meaningful congressional ethics reform, including restrictions on stock trading (must be in a blind trust) and not participating in prediction markets by members of Congress, while making affordability and the cost of living a central priority.
The Democratic victory was a mandate to address affordability and restore accountability, not a blank check for partisan retaliation. That doesn't mean ignoring wrongdoing or looking the other way when federal laws have been violated. Congress has a responsibility to conduct oversight, and no administration should be above the law. But investigations must be grounded in evidence and focused on legitimate misconduct, rather than becoming a substitute for governing.
Americans are tired of watching Washington investigate itself while their bills keep getting higher. They deserve a Congress capable of doing more than assigning blame.
* * *
## Shrinking Veteran Leadership in Congress
Here's a blurb from our friends at the Nimitz Report I found alarming: "Veterans are [expected to account for approximately 15% of the incoming Congress](https://substack.com/redirect/81f15f36-b57d-4893-bbe5-435052362014?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), down from 19% in the current Congress and potentially the lowest share since at least the 1970s. According to Military Times, at least 57 veterans had secured seats as of November 5, with additional races still undecided...The incoming Congress will include both returning veteran lawmakers and newly elected members with military backgrounds."
## Veterans Day Engagements this Week & Next Month
First off, Happy 251st Birthday to our legendary US Marine Corps today - which was founded in Tun Tavern in Philadelphia, PA, on November 10, 1775. Tomorrow is Veterans Day, and as many of you know, we're passionate about providing access to capital for the next generation of 'vetrepreneurs' \- as a venture capitalist (over $300 million invested), lecturer at Wharton (Huntsman Hall named after a Navy Veteran), and entrepreneur myself. Leaders solve problems and when 50% of World War II veterans came home and started their own small business but it's now less than 5% of Post 9/11 veterans who do so, there's a lot of work we have to do.
Pretty excited to be heading back down to Walmart in Bentonville, Arkansas to share the stage with the Walmart CEO John Furner, who started as an hourly associate and now leads 2.1 million associates around the world - as well the UHP (Unlock Human Potential) founder Matt Heese, an Army Veteran who runs one of the country's largest skill trades academies. It's especially ironic to be there on Veterans Day as Walmart's founder Sam Walton was a WWII veteran who founded the world's largest retailer. Lastly, this Thursday night we'll be at the US Chamber of Commerce Hiring Our Heroes Gala as the presenter giving out the Capital One Small Business Award (can't tell you who's receiving it yet, I don't know until I open up the envelope).
I mention these events because it's about building trust with all of you - every day, every week, and every month - not just on holidays like tomorrow. If you can, join us next month as we have our 5th annual [Army Navy Policy Conference](https://substack.com/redirect/9b1c5d2d-466e-4a85-a9f3-a25b28006b2c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Friday, December 11th at Fordham Business School (it's the day before the iconic Army Navy Game).
**And as a thank-you to our subscribers, you can attend free using the code PJM/G9.**
We're bringing together more than 200 leaders for an afternoon of conversation, collaboration, and networking. Our goal is to create a room where roughly one-third of attendees come from the senior military and veteran leadership community, one-third are cadets, junior officers, and emerging leaders, and one-third are executives, investors, and industry experts. It's an opportunity for the next generation to learn directly from those who have led in uniform, business, and public service--and for all of us to build relationships that can make a difference long after the conference ends.
We'll have an extraordinary lineup of leaders from the military, technology, finance, and national security communities, including Oracle CEO Mike Sicilia, alongside senior military and industry executives. The program will explore everything from defense technology and entrepreneurship to finance, media, and the opportunities available to veterans after service.
Hope you'll be part of the next generation of leaders who truly do what they can to earn your trust again...Go Army and Happy birthday Marines!

The DLCC is on the front lines, tracking more than **_100 races_** where recounts may be needed. These races include districts in battlegrounds like Minnesota, New Hampshire, and many others. Here’s how we help:
* **Help fund and support the legal costs** associated with recounts.
* **Work directly with teams on the ground** to provide guidance on how to navigate the process.
* **Coordinate with national partners** to understand which recounts have the highest stakes.
* **Focus our efforts where they matter most,** prioritizing races where recounts could make a real difference in the outcome of a race.

body:
This Veterans Day, hear Jim Caviezel’s powerful message on faith, freedom, sacrifice, and the responsibility we all share for America’s future.

### November 10, 2026 Newsletter
---
| | Jim Caviezel: A Candid Conversation on America & Ghost Soldier
---
| [](https://momsforamerica.us/so/31Q75vBEj/c?w=KgW-OOxjgs1Mk1UNULS-fMhorGtveKtoMQ-cXBty5NA.)
---
| | This Veterans Day, join Debbie Kraulidis for a special conversation with award-winning actor Jim Caviezel, best known for his roles in The Passion of the Christ and Sound of Freedom. Jim joins us to discuss his latest film, Ghost Soldier, a modern-day David and Goliath story about courage, conviction, and standing up for what is right. He shares what drew him to the story, how his faith influences the roles he chooses, and why Hollywood needs more stories that celebrate heroism, sacrifice, and the fight for freedom. As we honor the men and women who have served our nation, Jim reminds us why courage, faith, and a willingness to stand for what is right still matter. Watch this special Veterans Day episode of the Moms for America Podcast on [YouTube](https://momsforamerica.us/so/31Q75vBEj/c?w=QFalwuBNoJ4nO-shhnuSlLmCEuGAkXnuxSTIZcghWJA.), [Rumble](https://momsforamerica.us/so/31Q75vBEj/c?w=QFalwuBNoJ4nO-shhnuSlLmCEuGAkXnuxSTIZcghWJA.), [Spotify](https://momsforamerica.us/so/31Q75vBEj/c?w=gCdakyhONOwnGXFHTqcTSxoZouadehXXbUyfX9gE3Tg.), and [Apple](https://momsforamerica.us/so/31Q75vBEj/c?w=pb_kN0VQyfZ2ZcFjfPfqmnIQYoouduccLzIG7aQ2WBk.).

| | The election results may have been disappointing, but America’s story is far from over. While many are trying to explain what went wrong, Moms for America Founder and President Kimberly Fletcher reminds us that the left has been playing the long game for decades, working its way into our schools, media, entertainment, and culture, influencing the hearts and minds of the next generation. Now is not the time to panic or give up. It is time for moms to stand firm, protect and educate their children with truth, get involved in their communities, and keep building a stronger America. Our long game goes back to the founding principles of faith, freedom, and personal responsibility. And our commitment to those values must continue.America is not lost. We must keep the faith, lock arms, and stand together for our families and the future of our nation. Mamas, our work is far from finished. [Read Kimberly's powerful message](https://momsforamerica.us/so/31Q75vBEj/c?w=XlNN-KC9ObmQMCiO0g_UtSfVyVQABMJNbCd2kdQYX9I.) and join Moms for America as we continue building a stronger coalition of mothers committed to faith, family, freedom, and America's future. _Top news and headlines from around the state, brought to you by The Robinson Report._
#### **[Bellows' Office Advises Lewiston to Withhold More City Hall Voting Video](https://substack.com/redirect/c767bfdb-9e5e-431b-a2cb-b935068aa259?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
The entire country was treated to a firsthand view of what "democracy" looks like in Lewiston, a.k.a. Little Mogadishu, thanks to a Freedom of Access Act request that lawfully obtained video of what appeared to be serial violations of the statutes governing the use of "aides" or translators for voters. The video also showed soon-to-be former State Rep., Lewiston City Councilor, and controversial landlord Scott Harriman leading a band of Maine People's Alliance miscreants on a militant jaunt through city hall -- a brazen violation of Maine's rules for electioneering too close to polling places. Rather than investigate these blatant violations of election integrity laws, Maine Secretary of State Shenna Bellows is spending her time trying to block the release of more video that would show more questionable activity by Democrat NGOs and their Somali clients.
Here's what the City of Lewiston said after we requested the remaining week of early voting video:
> "The Maine Secretary of State's Office has advised the City that, because official ballots are visible in portions of the recording, release is prohibited by 21-A M.R.S. § 22(2), which provides that official ballots, including ballots in electronic or image format, are not public records and may be inspected only as authorized by Title 21-A. Although ballot markings are not discernible through ordinary viewing of the recording, the City cannot exclude the possibility that ballot information could be recovered through image enhancement. Accordingly, the City is withholding that portion of the recording pursuant to 21-A M.R.S. § 22(2)."
In other words, the Maine Secretary of State's Office has taken the position that some magical technology has been invented that can enhance grainy security camera footage to the point where you can read how the people in these images are voting. Notwithstanding the fact that _we all know how they are voting,_ the position is technologically and scientifically illiterate. The Secretary of State is, once again, willing to believe something that is utterly false and laughably implausible if it suits her world view and promotes her political power.
Two full images (with no zoom or enhancement) from the Lewiston security camera video that offer the best possible vantage point for creating the scenario the Secretary of State's office imagines.
Now let's use some standard enhancement and zooming tools to show the limits of what is possible to extract from this video file:
Traditional zoom and enhancement techniques show the implausibility of the Secretary's rationale for blocking the release of further video showing Democrat NGOs and their Somali clients ballot harvesting.
But let's go even further and use the best "Super Intelligence" models available to see if we can enhance these images even further to extract from the video files some data that is even there. Here's what's Silicon Valley's best frontier models can do to test Bellows' theory for blocking the release of video showing her friends and allies violating the state's election rules:
Magically enhanced video stills
The city admits "ballot markings are not discernible through ordinary viewing of the recording," but the city "cannot exclude the possibility that ballot information could be recovered through image enhancement."
Well, now they can.

#### **[UMaine Offers Voluntary Retirement Packages to 158 Faculty Members Amidst $19M Budget Shortfall](https://substack.com/redirect/55a2c3af-9c94-48e9-a138-8cac23da8938?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Who could have seen this coming? After decades of subsidizing quasi-mandatory college educations for every C- student in America to study queer theory or sports management, the U.S. economy has produced a massive oversupply C- professors -- and now that bubble is popping. At least, that's my read on the news that UMaine professors who are at least 55 with 10 years in, are being offered buyout packages. The offer goes to 158 faculty as the flagship stares at a projected $19 million hole for next year. Administrators blame flat tuition and federal changes to research money and international enrollment, and say layoffs are still coming, though nobody will say how many. Augusta certainly isn't in a position to bail out the college system, given that the 133rd State Legislature is about to inherit a $1,000,000,000 deficit caused almost entirely by bloated and defrauded welfare.
#### **[Jeffries Declares Democrats' Opposition To Working With Stephen Miller, Trump Admin's 'Extremism'](https://substack.com/redirect/fcba38ad-39b4-4fd2-9f20-e23bf76c8df0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
The man likely to be the next speaker of the House says the White House's new chief of staff gets no phone calls. Hakeem Jeffries told ABC's "This Week" there will be no "opportunity" to work with American hero Stephen Miller, after posting Friday that Miller's "presence in government should be eradicated like a malignant tumor." So much for the healing. For what it's worth, Jeffries has his metaphors mixed up: Stephen Miller is the radiation, the chemo, the miracle antidote to the cancerous rot of the American Republic. Dylan Kresak of the Daily Caller News Foundation has the story.
#### **[White House Staffers Undermined Pesticide Reform Over 'National Security,' Former MAHA Adviser Alleges](https://substack.com/redirect/ee3ae502-cc9e-439b-9ff1-9e041294c6b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

name: Chris Deluzio
subject: “Trickle-down economics” is a scam.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Deluzio for Congress
body:
And it must be crushed
# [](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/46?t=1&akid=166%2E42639%2EyuXMJW)
With last week's wins across our Commonwealth and across our country, Democrats have the chance to break corrupt corporate power, get their money out of our politics, and crush the scam that is "trickle-down economics."
But, unfortunately, this is that time when many of the politicians who take that corporate money stop talking ... and yes, that includes some Democrats.
They don't want to name the villains in this story.
But the American Dream did not just disappear.
Whether we call them robber barons or oligarchs, the corrupt and powerful have been ripping away the American Dream for decades.
They've consolidated huge monopolies.
They've hoarded enormous wealth for themselves.
They've cheered on lousy trade deals.
At the same time: Workers’ paychecks fell. Small businesses get crushed. Jobs shipped overseas. And the costs go up for all of us.
Then, those *villains* pour billions and billions of dollars into elections to protect an economy rigged for their benefit ... propped up by a corrupt system of campaign finance.
The result is what we've all seen. The robber barons, the oligarchs ... they get bought and paid for politicians to give them tax giveaways and saddle all of us with generationally crippling debt.
They call it trickle-down economics, but we know what it is.
It's a scam.
And if we have the courage -- and we must -- it can end on our watch, and we can create a government and an economy that works for all of us and not just the oligarchs and robber barons of this country.
Let's get it done.
Don't give up the ship,
Chris Deluzio

This is the closest House race in the entire country, and it could also be one of the most important.

As Chair of the Rules Committee, Virginia Foxx directly blocked the House from voting on Trump’s tariffs and the release of the Epstein files. ## **The 411 on the Lame-Duck Session**
Congress is back in Washington, and the clock is officially ticking. The lame-duck session is upon us, and there is zero time to waste.
Between now and January 3, 2027, when the new Congress is sworn in, Senate leadership and the White House must get crystal clear on their top priorities. The simple math of Capitol Hill dictates that once the clock runs out, any unconfirmed nominee or unfinished piece of conservative legislation dies.

There are two non-negotiables that must be executed over these final weeks:
* **Clear the Judicial & Executive Nominees: **Priority appointments - ambassadors, deputy secretaries, key agency directors, and federal judges - must be fast-tracked immediately. President Trump says there are 161 unconfirmed positions -- prioritize them.
* **Pass Essential & Conservative Legislation: **Beyond must-pass items like government funding and the National Defense Authorization act (NDAA), key legislative wins like the SAVE America Act and codifying border security policies must be pushed over the finish line.

The Senate cannot operate on a casual schedule of two-day workweeks and mid-session retreats. Lawmakers need to be working 24 hours a day, 7 days a week through January 3. As legendary coach Bill Belichick famously put it: _Do your job._
I get thats more work that most senators are used to but you ran for this office -- take Thanksgiving and Christmas off -- but that's it.
Today's issue breaks down why this lame-duck window is our last bite at the apple, how Chuck Schumer plans to stall every nominee, and the exact steps leadership must take right now.
